title: Fire Captain Omelette Bar
subtitle: Made-to-order omelettes with a prep line of fillings for ten.
description: A station-style omelette bar keeps the captain happy and the line moving: prepped fillings, beaten eggs in pitchers, and two pans running staggered. Everyone builds their own combo while the cook focuses on fold technique and heat control.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.notes: beaten in batches of 3 per omelette

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.notes: for pans, plus oil as needed

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Fire Captain Omelette Bar in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep the filling line
steps.instruction: Set all fillings in labeled hotel pans with spoons. Sauté mushrooms and peppers ahead; drain tomatoes well. Beat eggs with milk in a pitcher for fast pours. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 20 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Heat two pans
steps.instruction: Heat two nonstick skillets over medium. Add a knob of butter until foaming but not brown. Work one omelette per pan for steady throughput. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook and fill
steps.instruction: Pour 3-egg portion into each pan, swirl to coat, and let set briefly. Add chosen fillings to one half when the top looks mostly set but still glossy. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Fold and plate
steps.instruction: Fold omelettes in half with a spatula and slide onto warm plates. Wipe pans quickly between batches if residue builds. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Keep the line moving
steps.instruction: Call orders two at a time, not ten at once. Hold finished omelettes in a 200°F oven uncovered for no more than 5 minutes before quality drops. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Post a simple order card at the line: pick three fillings max so the cook doesn't get buried.
Run two pans staggered—pour pan B while folding pan A to maintain a steady rhythm.
Keep a damp towel and oil brush at the station for quick pan resets between omelettes.
cleanupNotes: Wipe nonstick pans with warm soapy water only after cooling—thermal shock warps lightweight pans.
Consolidate leftover fillings into labeled containers for omelette scrambles the next morning.
leftovers: Chop leftover omelettes into a breakfast fried rice with soy, green onion, and sesame oil.
Combine extra fillings with beaten eggs and bake as a frittata at 375°F for 25 minutes.
